# Lab 12.3: Feature Engineering with TRANSFORM

## What We Are Going to Do
Put preprocessing (scaling, bucketing, feature crosses) inside the model with the TRANSFORM clause, so prediction uses exactly the same logic.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Train with TRANSFORM.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL lab12.income_lr_tf
TRANSFORM (
  ML.STANDARD_SCALER(age) OVER () AS age_scaled,
  ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(hours_per_week, 5) OVER () AS hours_bucket,
  ML.FEATURE_CROSS(STRUCT(education, occupation)) AS edu_x_job,
  workclass, marital_status, sex,
  income_bracket
)
OPTIONS (model_type = 'LOGISTIC_REG', input_label_cols = ['income_bracket'], auto_class_weights = TRUE)
AS
SELECT age, hours_per_week, education, occupation, workclass, marital_status, sex, income_bracket
FROM `bigquery-public-data.ml_datasets.census_adult_income`;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Compare with Lab 12.2.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT 'basic' AS model, roc_auc FROM ML.EVALUATE(MODEL lab12.income_lr)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'transform', roc_auc FROM ML.EVALUATE(MODEL lab12.income_lr_tf);</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Predict with raw columns.** You pass raw `age` and `hours_per_week`. The model applies the same scaling and buckets automatically.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT predicted_income_bracket
FROM ML.PREDICT(MODEL lab12.income_lr_tf,
  (SELECT 45 AS age, 50 AS hours_per_week, ' Bachelors' AS education, ' Exec-managerial' AS occupation,
          ' Private' AS workclass, ' Married-civ-spouse' AS marital_status, ' Male' AS sex));</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[SQL] See the transformed features.**

<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT * FROM ML.TRANSFORM(MODEL lab12.income_lr_tf,

5. **[Console] Open the model's Schema tab.** It lists the transform outputs as the model's features.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| TRANSFORM | Preprocessing stored in the model |
| Training/serving skew | Avoided, same logic both times |
| `ML.TRANSFORM` | Shows engineered features |
| Note | Census strings start with a space |
